tier_reason: The harness is public: bench/bench.zig, bench/runners/pugixml_runner.cpp, bench/runners/rapidxml_runner.cpp, bench/runners/run_parse.zig and tools/scripts.zig (pugixml pinned to a git revision, rapidxml 1.13). The page states Zig 0.16.0 ReleaseFast -Dcpu=native, C++ flags -O3 -DNDEBUG -march=native, and the i5-12450H CPU. It misses A only because the baseline C++ compiler is recorded as the unnamed system 'c++' driver: no GCC or Clang identity and no version, in the page, latest.md or latest.json. That matches how earlier batches treated a missing compiler identity, so first-party numbers with partial methodology are C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: bench/README.md stable snapshot: ours-permissive DOM is 1.46x-9.73x faster than the best of {pugixml, rapidxml} on each of the 24 headline fixtures (24/24 PASS). On the 15 real-world and pugixml-corpus fixtures the range is 1.47x-5.41x; pugixml_large.xml runs at 2560.26 MiB/s vs pugixml 473.25 MiB/s (5.41x). The 8.88x and 9.73x top end comes from synthetic_tiny_empty ('<x/>' x220,000) and synthetic_tiny_text ('<x>a</x>' x120,000). Those inputs hit special-case exact-repeat DOM paths in src/parser.zig (detectRepeatedSelfClosingDocument, detectRepeatedSimpleTextPlan). The README average is 3799.40 MiB/s vs pugixml 1312.83 MiB/s, about 2.9x (derived from page data). The validated DOM averages 2037.12 MiB/s, about 1.55x pugixml (derived from page data), and it is slower than pugixml on weekly_utf8.xml (1218.10 vs 2151.54) and synthetic_deep_tree.xml (1124.84 vs 1259.10).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: zxml: Zig 0.16.0, ReleaseFast -Dcpu=native. pugixml (pinned git revision) and rapidxml 1.13: the unnamed system 'c++' driver (GCC or Clang not identified, no version), -O3 -DNDEBUG -march=native.
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark. The C++ baseline compiler is not identified (only the system 'c++' driver). Headline numbers use the default permissive, destructive DOM, which may reject a literal '>' inside a quoted attribute value; the full-grammar validated mode is much slower (mean 2037.12 MiB/s) and loses to pugixml on weekly_utf8.xml and synthetic_deep_tree.xml. The top of the range (8.9x-9.7x) comes from synthetic exact-repeat fixtures that trigger special-case repeated-token DOM fast paths. The pugixml runner uses load_buffer, which copies the input inside the timed loop, while rapidxml runs non-destructive. The project's VALIDATION.md says its own absolute throughput targets (>5 GiB/s permissive, >3 GiB/s validated) FAIL. The repo has 0 stars and is about 6 months old, so adoption is unproven.

notes: Every number in the record matches bench/README.md; the 3799.40 and 1312.83 averages are in the root README and VALIDATION.md. The record's 'first commits ~2026-09 / <2-week-old repo' is wrong: the repo was created 2026-04-03 and has about 290 commits. License MIT, not a fork, not archived, last commit 2026-09-09, active: all confirmed. If the orchestrator accepts a named project compiler plus flags without the C++ driver's identity, this entry would qualify as A. Every other part of the methodology (pinned baselines, CPU, kernel, source SHA-256s) is unusually rigorous.
